### Problem

Sparrow uses PurRDF's native governed SPARQL engine over a persisted `FallibleDatasetView` that advertises `storage_live_budget()` and supplies certified owned-term bounds and workspace reservations. Basic projected SELECT/BGP queries work, but broader graph queries required for agent troubleshooting are refused.

At inspected revision `3b6ec4d9f76984b62c0b07ede69cdd98baf813f5`, [bounded_workspace.rs](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf/blob/3b6ec4d9f76984b62c0b07ede69cdd98baf813f5/crates/sparql-eval/src/engine/bounded_workspace.rs) explicitly refuses:

- ASK, CONSTRUCT and DESCRIBE (only SELECT is admitted).
- Explicit active datasets.
- Solution modifiers and algebra outside Project(Bgp), including GRAPH, OPTIONAL, UNION, FILTER, BIND, grouping, ordering and property paths.
- Prebound substitutions and configured extension contexts, including property functions and focus-graph configuration.
- Nested RDF triple patterns, including otherwise basic projected SELECT/BGP queries containing a triple term.

These produce `native-sparql-workspace-unpriced`. Resident views take the zero-reservation path without this restriction. This is an admission gap beneath the existing parser/evaluator.

Existing reproduction: [segmented_query.rs](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf/blob/3b6ec4d9f76984b62c0b07ede69cdd98baf813f5/crates/sparql-eval/tests/segmented_query.rs), `tiny_capacity_and_unpriced_order_refuse_before_any_row_probe_or_output`, verifies that adding ORDER BY to an otherwise admitted query yields this diagnostic before any row probe. The guards were verified by source inspection; PurRDF's full gate was not rerun for this issue. Sparrow currently pins `e58974e504b9681597faea1490002ce8ddaf7448`; current PurRDF source still contains the restriction.

### Proposed solution

Complete native workspace admission for SELECT, ASK, CONSTRUCT, DESCRIBE, explicit default/named datasets, GRAPH and the existing algebra/operator surface. Support prepared substitutions and admitted native extension contexts, especially text property functions for graph/text correlation. Apply the same contract to operational EXPLAIN and direct/prepared/governed entries.

Reserve before execution allocations and retain admission through intermediate bags, result materialization and publication. Preserve typed operational failures, governor evidence, cancellation and budget exhaustion. Real resource refusals remain necessary when a query exceeds its admitted budget; selecting a supported query form/operator must not require an unbounded resident copy.

Sparrow owns persisted storage, retention, pins and ingestion coordination. PurRDF owns SPARQL semantics, text functions, scoring and governors. Do not suppress the storage budget, use no-op reservations, copy private evaluator code downstream or add a second engine. No feature flags or fabricated vocabulary defaults are requested.

### Acceptance

- Healthy bounded operational views match resident results for all four query forms, default/named/empty graphs, GRAPH, joins, OPTIONAL/BIND correlation, UNION, expressions, modifiers, aggregates, subqueries and property paths, including RDF 1.2 terms and solution-bag semantics.
- Direct, prepared and governed entries agree, including substitutions; admitted native text property functions and focus-graph configuration work on the bounded view.
- Operational EXPLAIN uses the view's cardinality evidence and admitted measuring execution, without an unpriced resident copy.
- Mid-read/checkpoint failures remain typed operational errors and outrank derived query diagnostics or governor trips. No answer or explanation is falsely published as complete.
- Independently test low workspace capacity, arithmetic overflow, cancellation, governor exhaustion and allocation failure. Reservations cover measured peak live execution/result ownership and are released on success and every failure path. Retained-result consumption holds its required admission.
- Add focused native regression and allocation tests, reuse shared test/measurement helpers, and pass the required PurRDF gate.

### Related work

#394 and #395 supplied fallible EXPLAIN and prepared/governed operational entries; this request concerns remaining bounded admission beneath those APIs. #481 concerns grouped-output allocation traffic and retains its narrower performance scope. Searches for WorkspaceUnpriced, bounded SPARQL and workspace admission found no issue covering this complete admission gap.

### Language surface(s)

Rust crate through existing public facade/native engine APIs.

# Complete bounded operational SPARQL

## Authority and delivery boundary

Deliver every requirement of the selected `issue.md` through the existing native evaluator. The accepted portfolio puts this complete sibling-enabling delivery first. Setup used `stagectl open` and `brief`; base is `3b6ec4d9f`. The issue has no comments. The brief searched fourteen other items, followed four linked issues within two hops, and identified three distinct historical GhpRsq defect classes in its last 200 records. Recurrence beyond that bounded coverage is UNKNOWN. No historical receipt qualifies the changed implementation.

Applicable authority: repository `AGENTS.md`, root `.baseline` and `.goals`, and `docs/design/purrdf-backend-contract.md`. No standalone ADR or constitution was found in the repository file inventory. Preserve all sibling worktrees and dirty layers; protect main. Rust tooling/tests, inherited lints, one implementation per job, deterministic output and RDF 1.2 semantics apply. No semantic feature or new runtime dependency. No suppressed storage ceiling, unbounded resident replay, second evaluator, global allocator substitution or unsafe lifetime extension. User authorization covers implementation, normal Stage issue/PR updates and protected integration through ghprsq. External-repository submissions are excluded.

The prior-art assessment maps reusable fallible publication, prepared/governed/EXPLAIN routes, segmented reservation and shared allocation probes. Previous narrow admission only proved SELECT Project(Bgp): deleting its guards would not prove full admission. A borrowed local reservation cannot cover retained raw result clones or extraction. Neither output optimization nor later physical spill work substitutes for this delivery.

## Chosen architecture

1. **One real query workspace owner.** Extend the static DatasetView contract with an explicit owned reservation capability for retained operational execution. Segmented reservations already own their Arc budget; resident execution keeps its erased no-op fast path. Forward the capability through every adapter/reference implementation and update custom native fixtures. Do not fabricate an owned guard from a borrowed RPIT return. The shared query admission owner holds its actual reservation, current admitted capacity and first typed resize refusal. A custom adapter may return a refusal without latching view status: preserve that typed cause and inspect it at publication. A pre-existing sticky view failure outranks the admission cause, which outranks derived evaluation errors/trips.

2. **Certified bounds where possible, growth admission where needed.** Replace the query-shape/input allowlist with a checked algebra admission walk. Known row/schema/planner/path/order/distinct/grouping/intermediate/output capacities receive checked bounds covering simultaneous owners and actual vector/hash capacity growth. Selective BGP probes remain selective; do not price every selective query as the whole dictionary. Cardinality used as a byte proof must cover the actual physical and virtual RDF stream, active default/named graph semantics and empty graph enumeration; add an explicit full-stream certificate if the existing quads-only cost hint is insufficient. Avoid double-counting segmented estimates that already include all tables. Overflow refuses before allocation rather than saturating a cost heuristic.

   Thread the live owner into EvalCtx and nested contexts, replacing marker-only admission. Stored-term size certificates apply only to stored values. At allocation owners, reserve before potentially unbounded computed string/arithmetic/aggregate/minted-value growth, substitution copies, term scratch and output staging. Owners either have a certified complete bound or use local checked pre-growth admission; after-the-fact scratch interning is insufficient. Use fallible capacity allocation and map its real failure to an actionable allocation diagnostic. Track coexisting pins, original allocations and replacement capacities; release only after the covered allocation is gone. Shared internal work gets one home, not parallel pricing implementations.

3. **Native producers price their actual work.** Extend the existing property-function/native extension admission seam with a workspace certificate or admitted pre-growth capability. Admitted native text search and occurrence relations cover needle analysis, full ranking when post-rank filters require it, ranking/intermediate/cursor buffers, bound-value copies, term rendering and emitted values. Pre-existing caller-owned index storage remains caller-owned. Row ceilings are neither byte certificates nor permission to truncate before a post-ranking filter. Preserve witnesses, ranking, modes and filtering. An opaque custom producer without the required certificate remains a truthful unadmitted producer; this must not be used to refuse supported built-in/native text paths. Apply the same law to configured functions/aggregates and nested calls that are admitted. Focus graph is the caller-supplied graph, never a synthesized resident copy of operational storage.

4. **Retained publication shares allocation and admission.** Introduce a retained operational payload distinct from the raw resident SparqlResult. It owns immutable shared payload plus the reservation covering that payload. Complete results, governed partial answers and operational EXPLAIN share their engine-owned allocation and lease on ordinary Clone. Ownership-carrying extraction keeps that lease. Do not expose a field move or engine-provided raw extraction that drops it. Keep borrowed immutable access for serializers and normal consumption; a caller explicitly copying borrowed values owns that new independent allocation. Do not attempt to police arbitrary client allocation. Update every real production consumer of changed APIs, including shared facade/host plumbing if compilation exposes it. Scoped visitor outputs owned by the visitor remain caller-owned; evaluator scratch remains admitted throughout the visitor and is released only after it is destroyed.

5. **One actual execution path and final checkpoint.** Wire direct, prepared, shared-operation governed, stop-signal and measured EXPLAIN entries to the same admission and retained-publication law. Remove obsolete bounded refusals only after their owners are priced. Keep configured standpoint/loss vocabulary behavior active on bounded storage, pricing actual copied configuration. Maintain cancellation, governor evidence, destination graph atomicity, bag/correlation semantics, and final source checkpoint precedence. No complete result/explanation or uncertified partial rows escape a failed source/checkpoint. Genuine governor partial answers retain their output admission.

Known costs: the owned capability and retained operational API require a coherent migration of native adapters/consumers. This is accepted GREENFIELD work; do not add a speculative compatibility engine. Declined: global allocator interception (not a sound library contract), whole-store admission for selective queries (defeats persisted selective storage), static stored-term multipliers for computed values (not a bound), and new optional features/dependencies (forbidden and unnecessary).

Segmented growth admission must use the same inclusive storage/cache/pin budget as initial admission, evicting eligible unpinned cache blocks where necessary. Avoid a strong-reference cycle between a retained owner and cached blocks. Bounded external adapters must supply an actual owned capability; a resident default may not silently become a no-op capability for a bounded adapter.

## Completeness contract and acceptance

All rows belong to Task 1, followed by qualification and publication in Task 2. Add or extend focused native fixtures under the existing support/test homes and reuse `purrdf_alloc_probe` and testkit. Compare actual payloads/bags/graphs to the resident oracle, not just success discriminants.

| Required behavior | Real execution and falsifiable check |
| --- | --- |
| SELECT, ASK, CONSTRUCT, DESCRIBE | Segmented persisted fixture and resident oracle through `query_fallible_view`, `query_prepared_fallible_view` and governed equivalents; exact boolean/solution bag/graph parity, retained graph and aux ownership |
| Complete supported algebra | Healthy bounded fixture exercises joins, GRAPH, OPTIONAL/BIND correlation, UNION, FILTER, expressions, ORDER/DISTINCT/REDUCED/Slice, aggregates/GROUP/HAVING, subqueries, MINUS/EXISTS and all supported property-path forms; exact resident parity |
| Active datasets and RDF 1.2 | Explicit FROM/FROM NAMED, default/named/remembered-empty graphs, graph enumeration, nested triple terms, reifiers, annotations, directional/language literals, duplicate solution bags and GlobalTermId beyond 2^53; full-stream cardinality certification and admitted virtual-heavy execution |
| Parameters/configuration | Prepared substitutions and direct inputs, focus graph, configured standpoint/loss vocabulary and admitted native functions/property functions/aggregates reach the actual configured implementation; expected resident parity |
| Native text | Real text index/search and occurrence relations correlate with graph rows; bound document/score/matched filters with LIMIT include a post-ranking-filter case, plus computed needle and long indexed subject/literal output; results and rank/truncation witness match resident behavior |
| EXPLAIN | Direct/prepared/options/stop-signal operational EXPLAIN runs against segmented view, reports its cardinality evidence and measured nodes; resident semantic agreement, no copy/replay; retained explanation keeps admission |
| Operational precedence | Mid-iterator, term materialization and final-checkpoint failures across direct/prepared/governed/scoped/EXPLAIN entries remain typed, outrank derived query error/cancel/trip, and publish no certified result; non-latching admission fixture verifies typed resize failure |
| Capacity and checked overflow | Low-capacity and overflowing row/byte certificates independently refuse before the affected allocation/probe, with capacity release and actionable typed/diagnostic cause; no saturating arithmetic or false completion |
| Cancellation/governor | Fired and mid-execution cancellation plus a real governor trip preserve receipts and partial-answer classification; compare resident semantics and retained partial lifetime; operational failure still wins |
| Allocation failure | Exercise an actual fallible capacity allocation failure independently of storage admission refusal; no panic, abort, invented success or mislabeled budget refusal, all earlier leases released |
| Live accounting | Thread-local shared allocator window measures simultaneous execution and owned result peak for every major operator family, growing CONCAT/REPLACE/arithmetic/GROUP_CONCAT values and text ranking; measured peak fits admitted session ledger without arbitrary unproved constants |
| Retained ownership | After return, keep complete/partial/explanation payload, ordinary clone and ownership-carrying extraction alive; the required reservation remains live until final covered owner drops. Repeated executions account simultaneous retained results. Errors and scoped completion release all covered allocations/charges |

## Task 1: Implement complete bounded native execution and retained egress

The fresh sole implementation agent changes the actual DatasetView/segmented/adapter contract, shared query workspace/admission walk, EvalCtx/allocation owners, native text/producer seams, complete/partial/EXPLAIN retained APIs and every affected production caller. Primary homes: `crates/rdf-core/src/dataset_view.rs`, segmented session and forwarding adapters; `crates/sparql-eval/src/{engine.rs,engine/,eval.rs,bgp.rs,scratch.rs,expr/,property_fn.rs,fallible.rs,governed.rs,governor/ledger.rs,execution.rs}` and actual allocation owners encountered by those production paths; `crates/text/src/{relation.rs,index.rs}` plus ranking owners; shared native fixtures/tests and affected consumers. Exact owner changes follow the certified-bound/pre-growth proof, not a blanket mechanical replacement.

NO DEFERRALS: Deliver every assigned requirement. If required behavior is missing or blocked, return Status: FAILED with the specific requirement and blocker. Do not report success for unfinished required work. Root continues actionable remedies rather than treating partial groundwork as issue completion.

Implement the coherent behavior and full focused acceptance together, then run affected-package checks through the bounded runner. No per-operator full gate, ceremonial review panel or baseline suite. Independent task review checks actual allocation owners, all callers, retained extraction/clone and the matrix evidence, writing `tasks/T1-review.md`. Resolve concrete findings, rerunning only invalidated checks. Normal signed commit and hooks, push and Stage issue update follow passing review/required qualification. Preserve selected Stage evidence separately from source.

## Task 2: Qualify, publish and integrate the complete delivery

Use `/opt/purrdf-508-qualification/run`: managed Rust toolchain, jobs/test threads 8, private target/build/temp and 64 GiB/no swap systemd scope. `validation.md` records commands, outcomes, coverage and limits. Maximum THREE full `make check` invocations across the entire issue→PR→main delivery, including failures; aim one after focused acceptance settles. Normal hooks are mandatory and never bypassed, weakened or killed. Full make check already includes wasm compilation; avoid a duplicate broad wasm campaign. Fix failures introduced/touched/depended on, report unrelated existing failures accurately.

After complete focused acceptance and substantive review, run the settled full required gate, create the issue-linked PR with `stagectl pr-create`, publish the plan and actual validation, and follow Stage 2/3 with proportional independent gap/completion and review-debt judgments. Retrieve actual hosted checks/review threads where the wrapper lacks complete coverage. Resolve actionable findings and prerequisites. Merge only with `/home/paudley/stage/root/bin/ghprsq --stage-dir` selecting this run, archive evidence and clean only this completed delivery. Local checks, hosted CI, source integration and registry publication are distinct. Do not claim the portfolio or this issue complete with missing acceptance.

The next portfolio batch is the clean current-main geo successor for complete 408/409. Only read-only preparation may overlap this source writer; at most one additional delivery awaiting CI/review. The frozen graph-default branch, all donor layers and excluded external submissions remain untouched.

The complete implementation is published in PR #526: https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf/pull/526.

Mandatory local `make check` attempt13 passed, including strict workspace/all-target checks, required hygiene and generated/license projections, native workspace runtime and documentation tests, and WASM release compilation. Both the source commit and normal main synchronization passed their signed hooks. Synchronization retained the exact full-qualified source while incorporating main's evaluated host-cost, temporal-cast and unrestricted TEXT contracts.

The final head is `2085e8647ceb871b5cdcbbdac99b869b03ca9979`; its actual main integration candidate is clean. Hosted CI and final review/integration acceptance remain pending, so issue508 is not complete. Earlier failed local invocations are retained honestly in the selected Stage evidence with their fixes and subsequent results; no scope cut, weakened physical ceiling or changed conformance golden is accepted.
